note: Opened on the simulation seat's request, whose user reversed an earlier hold. The bridge opened nothing by itself. The round was written only after the ledger's hash stopped covering status (af5353b): before that, the approval this plan is due to receive would have made a correctly transported round report tampering. Delivered to microscope_agent/inbox/ under 7.1 rule 8; until that path existed the turn pointed at a side with no way to see the round. Held on the sample mismatch the microscope seat found in the delivery and declined to reconcile, which was right -- taking either value would have had one side silently measuring a different sample, and the bridge may not choose between them either (4.4). Out of held on two facts already on disk, neither of them this seat's choice. The round was taken: microscope_agent/questions/mic-20260919-001/goal.json carries from_round for this round at VALIDATED (b286d1e), which is the only signal 7.1 rule 8 leaves instead of a reply, and it had stood unread in this ledger for an hour. And the hold's reason was discharged by the person: plan.md 11-13 (121514e) aligns both sides now on the value a claim carries rather than the one a placeholder does, which is exactly the harm the hold was written against -- two samples run as one comparison. The carried payload has not moved. plan-sim-20260917-001 stands at revision 1 with the placeholder, and both ledger hashes still re-derive from disk. Applying 11-13 to a card in flight is not this seat's to do; the revision belongs to the side that wrote the card. When it lands, check 8 stops counting this round as verified rather than failing -- the source moved on -- and the envelope already in the microscope's inbox becomes a parcel the contract has no way to mark as superseded, since a second round for one (direction, observable) is not open to this thread and nothing may be removed from an inbox. Raised with the bridge manager. Moved before the handover was written. tasks/001 still has this thread belonging to bridge-2 and moves a thread only when the move is written there; bridge and bridge-2 are both closed in the registry, this seat is bridge-3 (9d1d943), and the person -- who asked the bridge manager for the written handover -- told this seat to commit meanwhile. The instruction came from the person rather than from another session, which is the distinction 6.2.2 draws, and it is recorded here and in the commit message because the message it arrived in will not survive. Values stay in the two cards; this ledger does not restate them.
